reference.source: Rook's Textbook of Dermatology / WHO Classification of Skin Tumours
clinicalPearls: A benign adnexal tumour with apocrine/eccrine differentiation, presenting as a firm smooth pink to red nodule usually on the scalp, head, or neck
Solitary lesions are usually sporadic; multiple confluent scalp nodules may coalesce into the classic turban tumour appearance
Multiplicity, especially with trichoepitheliomas and spiradenomas, points to CYLD-related Brooke-Spiegler syndrome
Histology shows islands of basaloid cells arranged in a jigsaw-puzzle pattern separated and surrounded by a thickened hyaline basement-membrane material
Droplets of hyaline basement-membrane material are also seen within the tumour nests, a helpful diagnostic clue
Germline or somatic loss of the CYLD tumour-suppressor deregulates NF-kB signalling and predisposes to these adnexal tumours
Most are benign, but long-standing or rapidly changing lesions can rarely undergo malignant transformation to cylindrocarcinoma
reference.pathophysiology: Cylindroma is a benign cutaneous adnexal neoplasm showing apocrine and eccrine differentiation. It is composed of nests and cords of basaloid epithelial cells arranged in an interlocking jigsaw-puzzle pattern, each nest sheathed by and interspersed with abundant hyaline basement-membrane material. Loss-of-function alterations in the CYLD gene, a tumour suppressor that normally restrains nuclear factor-kappa B signalling by removing regulatory ubiquitin chains, deregulate this pathway and promote survival and proliferation of the adnexal cells. When CYLD is affected in the germline, patients develop multiple cylindromas, spiradenomas, and trichoepitheliomas as part of Brooke-Spiegler syndrome, whereas sporadic solitary lesions may harbour somatic CYLD changes.
additionalInvestigations: Excisional or incisional biopsy with histopathology demonstrating the jigsaw pattern and hyaline sheaths
Clinical mapping of the scalp and head-neck region for multiple lesions
Family history and examination for spiradenomas and trichoepitheliomas
CYLD genetic testing when Brooke-Spiegler syndrome is suspected
Imaging of extensive confluent scalp disease to plan surgery
redFlags: Rapid growth, ulceration, or bleeding of a previously stable nodule suggesting malignant transformation
Extensive confluent turban-tumour disease causing functional or cosmetic morbidity
Family clustering of adnexal tumours indicating a hereditary syndrome
reference.prognosis: Cylindromas are benign and slow-growing with an excellent prognosis after excision; syndromic patients develop numerous recurrent lesions requiring repeated intervention, and malignant transformation, though rare, carries a more serious outlook.
pitfalls: Misinterpreting the histology as adenoid cystic carcinoma or basal cell carcinoma
Overlooking the syndromic context when multiple adnexal tumours are present
Failing to recognise features of malignant change in long-standing lesions
Incomplete excision of confluent lesions leading to recurrence
